BA.rationale: Boeing's fundamental health is severely impaired: the company is barely profitable on a net basis (Q1 2026 net income of -$7M, EPS -$0.11), with razor-thin gross margins of 4.8% and operating margins of 4.6%. The balance sheet is deeply strained with total equity of only $5.99B against $46.96B in debt (debt-to-equity of 7.84x), and operating cash flow was negative -$179M in Q1 2026. The trajectory shows some improvement year-over-year (revenue +14% YoY) but sequential deterioration (QoQ revenue -2.3%, EPS -88%). Valuation is extremely stretched at a P/E of 72.9x and P/B of 27.5x for a company with these fundamentals. Multiple near-term headwinds exist: 777X certification delays potentially into the late 2020s, ongoing 737 MAX production caps at 47/month, supply chain bottlenecks, DOJ criminal exposure for breaching the 2021 DPA, and China delivery disruptions. The FAA's restoration of self-certification authority (July 20) is a modest positive but doesn't address the structural issues. Earnings on July 28 could be a catalyst but the risk is skewed to the downside given persistent operational challenges.
